# Walkthrough Scope

## How To Build

A WalkthroughScope should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A WalkthroughScope should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, intergration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../ui/theme/index.md#theme-scope): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Concept

### Pitch

A guided walkthrough that takes a new user from nothing to a project of their own, then through the prompt modes one by one, pointing at each part of the window as it explains it, so the first prompt is sent knowing what each mode does.

### Shape

#### Description

The walkthrough is a series of steps, each pointing at one part of the window with a spotlight and explaining it in a callout. It never sends a prompt or changes anything but what the user does at its bidding, as creating the project, and what it selects to show, as a ribbon tab or a chat input tab.

#### Spotlight

While a step shows, the window is dimmed, as an inset panel dims it, but for a cut-out around the part the step points at, with 4 pixels of room and corners rounded 6 pixels, outlined in the theme's accent, so that part reads as lit. The cut-out moves to each step's part, easing between them over 200 milliseconds, and follows it if the window is resized.
Beside it sits the callout, a card on the theme's raised surface with corners rounded 8 pixels, a border, and a shadow, at most 320 pixels wide, placed on whichever side of the part has room, with a small pointer toward it, and never off the window. It holds the step's title, its text as a paragraph or two, "Step N of M", muted, and along its bottom a Back button, disabled on the first step, a primary Next button, reading "Done" on the last step, and a "Skip tour" link at the left. It is drawn in the theme's roles, in dark mode and light.
While a step shows, only the callout and the part lit take the mouse, and clicks on the dimmed window do nothing, so the walkthrough is never left by accident. <Escape> skips the tour, as Skip tour does, and <Enter>, while Next is enabled, goes to the next step.

#### Steps

The steps, in order, each selecting what it points at before it shows, as opening the Project tab of the ribbon, expanding the ribbon first if it is collapsed:

- "Projects live here", the Project tab of the ribbon, opened: a project is a folder holding its spec, its code, and a piton.config.pi that says where each is, and everything Suspense does, it does in the project open.
- "Create a project", the New Project button of the [RibbonProjectTabScope](../../ui/components/ribbon/project-tab/index.md#ribbon-project-tab-scope): it asks for the project to be created. Next is disabled, and the step goes on by itself once the New Project form opens, as clicking the button opens it. Where a project is already open, the callout also offers "Use the open project", which skips to the prompt modes with it.
- "Fill it in", the New Project form, as the [NewProjectScope](../new-project/index.md#new-project-scope) says, lit whole, the callout beside the panel, above it: it names the project, where it goes, the template it starts from, and the agents it is written for, and says the defaults are a fine start. Next is disabled; the step goes on by itself once the project is created and opens. Cancelling the form goes back to the step before.
- "Every prompt has a mode", the tabs of the [ChatInputScope](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope): what is typed below is sent in the mode of the tab selected, and each mode does a different kind of work.
- "Code", the Code tab, selected: changes the code to do what the prompt asks, reading the spec to know how, and leaves the spec as it is. Code tasks run on this machine, in the project.
- "Spec", the Spec tab, selected: changes the spec, the description of what the application should be, and leaves the code as it is, so a change can be agreed on before anything is built. Spec tasks run in a container that holds only the spec, and the spec is built after each.
- "Code and Spec", the Chain tab, selected, Code and Spec together: changes the spec first, then hands it to a code step that changes the code to match, one prompt doing both. It is where the chat input starts, and the usual way to ask for a change.
- "Ask", the Ask tab, selected: asks a question about the code and the spec, changing neither, and answers beside the tasks, as the [AskConversationScope](../prompt-mode/ask-conversation/index.md#ask-conversation-scope) shows; questions run straight away, never waiting behind tasks.
- "You're ready", the chat input's text box: type a prompt, pick its mode, and send it. The walkthrough can be taken again from Walkthrough, in the Application tab.

Each mode's step reads in that mode's colour, its title and its outline, as the [PromptModesScope](../prompt-mode/modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope) colours it. Back goes to the step before, selecting again what it selects, but never back into the steps that create the project once it has been created.

#### Ending

Done, on the last step, ends the walkthrough, leaving the chat input on the Chain tab, as it starts, with keyboard focus in its text box. Skip tour ends it straight away, at any step, leaving everything as it is. Either way the dimming goes, and the walkthrough is remembered as taken for the user, as the [UserPreferencesScope](../user-preferences/index.md#user-preferences-scope) says, so it is never offered again by itself.

#### Starting

The walkthrough starts by itself only once for a user, until it has been taken or skipped: when the [WelcomeScope](../welcome/index.md#welcome-scope)'s Get started is pressed, or, where the welcome page doesn't open at launch because everything is ready, once the window has opened. It can be taken again at any time with the Walkthrough command, a "Walkthrough" button with a signpost icon in the Help group of the [RibbonApplicationTabScope](../../ui/components/ribbon/application-tab/index.md#ribbon-application-tab-scope), after Welcome, whose tooltip says it walks through creating a project and the prompt modes. It is a full button, and not primary. Started with a project open, it starts at its first step all the same, offering "Use the open project" at the second.
It never starts over an inset panel, but waits for it to close, and it isn't offered while work is running; started from its command, it closes any inset panel open first.

content.text:
The walkthrough is in. It dims the window except for a highlighted cut-out around each part in turn, with a callout card beside it. It runs from the Project tab through creating a project, then explains Code, Spec, Code and Spec, and Ask one at a time. All 498 tests pass, but I haven't run it in the actual app, so I haven't seen the overlay or the 200 ms glide on screen.

**How it works:**
- **Steps:**
  - "Projects live here" opens the Project tab, expanding the ribbon first if it's collapsed.
  - "Create a project" moves on by itself once the New Project form opens. If a project is already open, it also offers "Use the open project", which skips to the modes.
  - "Fill it in" moves on to the modes once the project is created. Cancelling the form goes back a step.
  - The four mode steps each select their tab and are drawn in that mode's colour. "Code and Spec" lights Code, the chain icon and Spec together.
  - "You're ready" lights the text box.
- **Moving through it:** Back is disabled on the first step and never returns to creating a project once one exists. Next reads Done on the last step and is disabled on the two steps that move on by themselves. Enter goes to the next step, Esc skips, and clicks on the dimmed area do nothing.
- **Ending:** Done leaves the Chain tab selected with the cursor in the text box. Done or Skip tour marks it as taken (remembered for the user) so it isn't offered again by itself.
- **Starting by itself:** once per user, either after "Get started" on the Welcome page or at launch when all the checks pass. If a floating panel is open, it waits for it to close.
- **Starting by hand:** a new "Walkthrough" button with a signpost icon, after Welcome in the Application tab's Help group. It closes any open panel first.

Where I made a call the spec doesn't spell out:
- **New Project form step:** the form fills almost the whole window, so the callout sits over the form near its bottom rather than beside it.
- **The callout's pointer** is a small square nub on the card's edge, because I couldn't rotate an element to make a proper arrow.
- **Back from "Fill it in"** closes the New Project form.
- **While work is running:** the Walkthrough button shows a short notice ("can be taken once the work running is over") rather than being disabled. If work is running when it would have started by itself, it just doesn't start, and since it isn't marked as taken it's offered again next launch.
- **"Projects live here"** lights the Project tab's label, not its whole row of commands.

The main code is in the new `src/walkthrough.rs`, with the step handling and keys in `src/main_window.rs`. The ribbon tab, New Project button, New Project form, chat tabs and text box now report their positions so the walkthrough can find them. The Welcome page's Get started button now has its own event so the walkthrough can follow it.
